decidable_of_iff'.code: decidable_of_iff' {a : Prop} (b : Prop) (h : a ↔ b) [Decidable b] : Decidable a
decidable_of_iff'.comment:
Transfer decidability of `b` to decidability of `a`, if the propositions are equivalent.
This is the same as `decidable_of_iff` but the iff is flipped.
decidable_of_iff'.fullDefinition: @[inline] def decidable_of_iff' (b : Prop) (h : a ↔ b) [Decidable b] : Decidable a :=   decidable_of_decidable_of_iff h.symm
decidable_of_iff'.description: The decidability of one proposition can be inferred from the decidability of another if the two propositions are equivalent.

Decidable.not_imp_not.code: Decidable.not_imp_not {a b : Prop} [Decidable a] : ¬a → ¬b ↔ b → a
Decidable.not_imp_not.description: The negation of one statement implies the negation of another if and only if the truth of the second statement implies the truth of the first.

exists_congr.code: exists_congr.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p q : α → Prop} (h : ∀ (a : α), p a ↔ q a) : (∃ a, p a) ↔ ∃ a, q a
exists_congr.description: The existence of an element satisfying one property is equivalent to the existence of an element satisfying another property if both properties are related by an equivalence for all elements.

decidable_of_iff.code: decidable_of_iff {b : Prop} (a : Prop) (h : a ↔ b) [Decidable a] : Decidable b
decidable_of_iff.comment:
Transfer decidability of `a` to decidability of `b`, if the propositions are equivalent.
**Important**: this function should be used instead of `rw` on `Decidable b`, because the
kernel will get stuck reducing the usage of `propext` otherwise,
and `decide` will not work.
decidable_of_iff.fullDefinition: @[inline] def decidable_of_iff (a : Prop) (h : a ↔ b) [Decidable a] : Decidable b :=   decidable_of_decidable_of_iff h
decidable_of_iff.description: The decidability of one proposition can be inferred from the decidability of another if they are equivalent.

and_iff_right.code: and_iff_right {a b : Prop} (ha : a) : a ∧ b ↔ b
and_iff_right.description: The conjunction of one statement with another is equivalent to the second statement alone provided the first statement is true.

exists_eq_left'.code: exists_eq_left'.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p : α → Prop} {a' : α} : (∃ a, a' = a ∧ p a) ↔ p a'
exists_eq_left'.description: The existence of an element satisfying a property in conjunction with being equal to a given element is equivalent to that element satisfying the property.

Exists.imp.code: Exists.imp.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p q : α → Prop} (h : ∀ (a : α), p a → q a) : (∃ a, p a) → ∃ a, q a
Exists.imp.description: If there exists an element satisfying one property, and that property implies another for all elements, then there exists an element satisfying the second property as well.

exists_and_left.code: exists_and_left.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p : α → Prop} {b : Prop} : (∃ x, b ∧ p x) ↔ b ∧ ∃ x, p x
exists_and_left.description: The existence of an element that satisfies a property alongside a condition is equivalent to that condition being true and the existence of an element satisfying the property.

and_left_comm.code: and_left_comm {a b c : Prop} : a ∧ b ∧ c ↔ b ∧ a ∧ c
and_left_comm.description: The conjunction of three propositions can be rearranged without changing the truth value, specifically switching the first two while keeping the third unchanged.

Exists.nonempty.code: Exists.nonempty.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p : α → Prop} : (∃ x, p x) → Nonempty α
Exists.nonempty.description: The existence of an element satisfying a property implies that there is at least one element in the set from which that element is drawn.

not_exists.code: not_exists.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p : α → Prop} : (¬∃ x, p x) ↔ ∀ (x : α), ¬p x
not_exists.description: The negation of the existence of an element satisfying a property is equivalent to the property being false for all elements.

exists_prop.code: exists_prop {b a : Prop} : (∃ (_ : a), b) ↔ a ∧ b
exists_prop.description: The existence of an element satisfying one proposition implies both that proposition and another proposition are true.

and_right_comm.code: and_right_comm {a b c : Prop} : (a ∧ b) ∧ c ↔ (a ∧ c) ∧ b
and_right_comm.description: The conjunction of two propositions combined with a third can be rearranged without changing the truth value, specifically moving the third proposition to the front while keeping the other two in their original order.

and_and_and_comm.code: and_and_and_comm {a b c d : Prop} : (a ∧ b) ∧ c ∧ d ↔ (a ∧ c) ∧ b ∧ d
and_and_and_comm.description: The conjunction of four propositions can be rearranged in such a way that the first two can switch places with one of the subsequent pairs without changing the truth value.

and_iff_left.code: and_iff_left {b a : Prop} (hb : b) : a ∧ b ↔ a
and_iff_left.description: The conjunction of a proposition with another that is known to be true is equivalent to the first proposition alone.

forall_const.code: forall_const.{u_1} {b : Prop} (α : Sort u_1) [i : Nonempty α] : α → b ↔ b
forall_const.description: For any nonempty type, a constant function to a proposition is equivalent to that proposition itself.

forall_exists_index.code:
forall_exists_index.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p : α → Prop} {q : (∃ x, p x) → Prop} :
  (∀ (h : ∃ x, p x), q h) ↔ ∀ (x : α) (h : p x), q ⋯
forall_exists_index.comment:
As `simp` does not index foralls, this `@[simp]` lemma is tried on every `forall` expression.
This is not ideal, and likely a performance issue, but it is difficult to remove this attribute at this time.
forall_exists_index.description: The ability to universally quantify over an existence statement implies that for every element satisfying a property, the subsequent property can also be universally quantified in relation to that element.

forall_apply_eq_imp_iff.code:
forall_apply_eq_imp_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Sort u_2} {β : Sort u_1} {f : α → β} {p : β → Prop} :
  (∀ (b : β) (a : α), f a = b → p b) ↔ ∀ (a : α), p (f a)
forall_apply_eq_imp_iff.description: The statement that for any function and property, the universal quantification of a condition holds if and only if the property can be expressed as a function applied to the variable from the domain.

exists_false.description: The statement asserting the non-existence of an element satisfying a false property indicates that no such element can exist.

exists_eq_right.code: exists_eq_right.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p : α → Prop} {a' : α} : (∃ a, p a ∧ a = a') ↔ p a'
exists_eq_right.description: The existence of an element satisfying a property and equating to a specific element is equivalent to that specific element satisfying the property.

forall_apply_eq_imp_iff₂.code:
forall_apply_eq_imp_iff₂.{u_1, u_2} {α : Sort u_2} {β : Sort u_1} {f : α → β} {p : α → Prop} {q : β → Prop} :
  (∀ (b : β) (a : α), p a → f a = b → q b) ↔ ∀ (a : α), p a → q (f a)
forall_apply_eq_imp_iff₂.description: The universal quantification of a property combined with an implication involving a function is equivalent to a direct universal quantification of the resulting property after applying the function to the initial condition.

forall_eq_or_imp.code:
forall_eq_or_imp.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p q : α → Prop} {a' : α} :
  (∀ (a : α), a = a' ∨ q a → p a) ↔ p a' ∧ ∀ (a : α), q a → p a
forall_eq_or_imp.description: The universal quantification of a condition leading to a proposition can be expressed as the conjunction of that proposition at a specific point and the same condition leading to the proposition for all points.

Decidable.or_iff_not_imp_left.code: Decidable.or_iff_not_imp_left {a b : Prop} [Decidable a] : a ∨ b ↔ ¬a → b
Decidable.or_iff_not_imp_left.description: The disjunction of one proposition with another is equivalent to asserting that if the first proposition is false, then the second must be true.

not_or.description: The negation of a disjunction is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual propositions.

or_self_iff.description: The disjunction of a proposition with itself is equivalent to the proposition alone.

exists_and_right.code: exists_and_right.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p : α → Prop} {b : Prop} : (∃ x, p x ∧ b) ↔ (∃ x, p x) ∧ b
exists_and_right.description: The existence of an element satisfying a property along with an additional proposition is equivalent to the existence of that element satisfying the property and the truth of the additional proposition.

forall_eq.code: forall_eq.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p : α → Prop} {a' : α} : (∀ (a : α), a = a' → p a) ↔ p a'
forall_eq.description: For any type, if a property holds for all elements equal to a specific element, then it holds for that specific element itself.

forall_and.code: forall_and.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p q : α → Prop} : (∀ (x : α), p x ∧ q x) ↔ (∀ (x : α), p x) ∧ ∀ (x : α), q x
forall_and.description: The universal quantification of a conjunction of two properties is equivalent to the conjunction of the universal quantifications of each property individually.

or_and_right.code: or_and_right {a b c : Prop} : (a ∨ b) ∧ c ↔ a ∧ c ∨ b ∧ c
or_and_right.description: The conjunction of a disjunction with another proposition is equivalent to the disjunction of the conjunctions of each component with that proposition.

Or.by_cases.code: Or.by_cases.{u} {p q : Prop} [Decidable p] {α : Sort u} (h : p ∨ q) (h₁ : p → α) (h₂ : q → α) : α
Or.by_cases.comment: Construct a non-Prop by cases on an `Or`, when the left conjunct is decidable.
Or.by_cases.fullDefinition: protected def Or.by_cases [Decidable p] {α : Sort u} (h : p ∨ q) (h₁ : p → α) (h₂ : q → α) : α :=   if hp : p then h₁ hp else h₂ (h.resolve_left hp)
Or.by_cases.description: This defines a method to derive a result from two possible situations based on the truth of a disjunction when one option is decidable, allowing a conclusion to be reached based on which disjunct is true.

and_or_left.code: and_or_left {a b c : Prop} : a ∧ (b ∨ c) ↔ a ∧ b ∨ a ∧ c
and_or_left.description: The conjunction of one proposition with the disjunction of two others is equivalent to the disjunction of the conjunction of the first proposition with each of the other two.

ite_not.code: ite_not.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} (p : Prop) [Decidable p] (x y : α) : (if ¬p then x else y) = if p then y else x
ite_not.comment: Negation of the condition `P : Prop` in a `ite` is the same as swapping the branches.
ite_not.description: The result of a conditional expression with a negated condition is equivalent to swapping the outcomes for the original condition.

eq_mpr_eq_cast.code: eq_mpr_eq_cast.{u_1} {α β : Sort u_1} (h : α = β) : h.mpr = cast ⋯
eq_mpr_eq_cast.description: The equality of two types allows for the equivalence between a specific form of equality and a type-casting operation.

forall_prop_of_false.code: forall_prop_of_false {p : Prop} {q : p → Prop} (hn : ¬p) : (∀ (h' : p), q h') ↔ True
forall_prop_of_false.description: If a proposition is false, then the universal quantification over another proposition derived from it is equivalent to asserting that the latter is always true.

and_self_iff.description: The conjunction of a proposition with itself is equivalent to the proposition itself.

And.imp.code: And.imp {a c b d : Prop} (f : a → c) (g : b → d) (h : a ∧ b) : c ∧ d
And.imp.description: If one can derive a second proposition from the first and a third proposition from a fourth, then given both original propositions, one can conclude the derived propositions.

exists_or.code: exists_or.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p q : α → Prop} : (∃ x, p x ∨ q x) ↔ (∃ x, p x) ∨ ∃ x, q x
exists_or.description: The existence of an element satisfying at least one of two properties is equivalent to the disjunction of the existence of elements satisfying each property separately.

decide_eq_false_iff_not.code: decide_eq_false_iff_not (p : Prop) : ∀ {x : Decidable p}, decide p = false ↔ ¬p
decide_eq_false_iff_not.description: The decision procedure for a proposition being false is equivalent to asserting that the proposition itself is false.

forall₂_congr.code:
forall₂_congr.{u_1, u_2} {α : Sort u_1} {β : α → Sort u_2} {p q : (a : α) → β a → Prop}
  (h : ∀ (a : α) (b : β a), p a b ↔ q a b) : (∀ (a : α) (b : β a), p a b) ↔ ∀ (a : α) (b : β a), q a b
forall₂_congr.description: The equivalence states that if two properties are related for all pairs of elements from a type and a dependent type according to a certain condition, then the universal quantifications of those properties are also equivalent.

exists_apply_eq_apply.code: exists_apply_eq_apply.{u_1, u_2} {α : Sort u_2} {β : Sort u_1} (f : α → β) (a' : α) : ∃ a, f a = f a'
exists_apply_eq_apply.description: There exists an element such that a function applied to that element is equal to the function applied to another specified element.

exists_imp.code: exists_imp.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p : α → Prop} {b : Prop} : (∃ x, p x) → b ↔ ∀ (x : α), p x → b
exists_imp.description: The implication of the existence of an element satisfying a property leading to a conclusion is equivalent to asserting that this conclusion holds for all elements that satisfy the property.

forall_congr'.code: forall_congr'.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p q : α → Prop} (h : ∀ (a : α), p a ↔ q a) : (∀ (a : α), p a) ↔ ∀ (a : α), q a
forall_congr'.description: The universal quantification of two propositions is equivalent if there is a correspondence between the propositions for every element in the set.

exists_eq_left.code: exists_eq_left.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p : α → Prop} {a' : α} : (∃ a, a = a' ∧ p a) ↔ p a'
exists_eq_left.description: The equivalence states that the existence of an element satisfying a specific property alongside its equality to a given element is equivalent to the property being satisfied by that given element.
